calls.title: Connect
calls.summary: The discussion addressed the absence of a current contract with Deal for existing EOR employees, hindering potential benefits like deposit waivers. Justin proposed a one-year agreement with early invoicing that would allow monthly billing of estimated costs instead of upfront deposits, thus easing cash flow issues. Jennifer expressed interest in this agreement but requested detailed contract terms and its implications for existing employees. Planned hires include a software engineer in Canada with future needs in EMEA and APAC based on candidate quality. Concerns over declining support quality were raised, particularly regarding conflicting information from the AI chatbot and human support. Transparent communication was emphasized to foster trust and collaboration, with a follow-up call scheduled to address outstanding questions about the contract and pricing.
calls.keywords: Employer of Record, Early Invoicing, International Hiring, Contract Agreement, Support Experience, Pricing Structure

calls.title: Connect
calls.summary: The meeting thoroughly discussed payment and deposit handling, explaining that deposits convert to deal balances when early invoicing is enabled, and refunds occur to a client's bank when EORs leave. Billing credits were delineated as usable for admin fees only, not withdrawable to bank accounts. The bank guarantee process outlined a 5-step timeline and semi-annual reviews, contrasting it with the quicker early invoicing method. Pricing negotiations highlighted a current EOR fee and potential discounts for multi-year contracts. The team emphasized contractual transparency, noting auto-renewal clauses are negotiable. Jennifer raised regulatory concerns regarding DOJ news, which Allison addressed by assuring no current impact on business operations. A follow-up meeting was scheduled to finalize decisions.
calls.keywords: Early Invoicing, Bank Guarantee, EOR Fees, Billing Credits, Multi-Year Contract, DOJ News
